Hello everyone. Before an international meeting, I always follow three steps. First, I decide what I want to achieve, and I write it in one sentence. Second, I practice saying my key points out loud. It sounds simple, but most people avoid doing it, and that is a mistake. Third, I consider what the other side might ask, and I prepare short answers. During the meeting, I try to speak slowly, and I never pretend to understand. If I miss something, I ask the speaker to repeat it. We can't afford to make decisions based on a misunderstanding. Finally, after the meeting, I offer to send a short summary. People appreciate it, and it keeps everyone on the same page.
